findings.title: Publish loose blobs through the existing durable namespace owner

sources.symbol: blobStore.prepare: existing loose/packed verification, staging Sync/Close, os.Rename and final SyncDirectory

findings.evidence: prepare flushes the staging file, closes it, calls os.Rename, then fsatomic.SyncDirectory. The Windows SyncDirectory implementation returns nil and explicitly requires namespace publication through Replace or a surviving-link SyncFile. Installed Go's os.rename delegates to windows.Rename, which uses MoveFileEx with MOVEFILE_REPLACE_EXISTING alone. commitCoordinator.commit then appends the referencing journal frame. Existing packBlobsUnder and backup publishers already call fsatomic.Replace, whose Windows owner requests write-through (and flushes its POSIX-rename fallback); Unix owner syncs affected directories. Unsupported assumption: plain rename plus a no-op supplies the same publication durability. Admitted scenario: a Windows Commit with external content (at least4096 bytes) succeeds and power is lost after the journal flush while the blob namespace move has not persisted. This lost-blob outcome is a hypothesis, not a reproduced incident. Official flag semantics: https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/windows/win32/api/winbase/nf-winbase-movefileexw .
findings.impact: Potential committed content loss after power interruption; subsequent OpenContent reports the missing required blob rather than recovering its bytes. This is a durability contract repair, not a speed optimization. No confidentiality issue established. Error-path retries also matter: existing loose files currently return after hash verification, so a prior publication/sync error must not be treated as proof of durable publication.
findings.recommended_change: Reuse fsatomic.Replace for the staging-to-destination transition in blobStore.prepare and remove its separate final SyncDirectory call. Keep payload hashing, conflicting-size/corrupt-orphan refusal, staging write/Sync/Close, error wrapping and cleanup. Before closing the finding, reconcile the existing-loose retry path after a namespace-persistence failure using the existing fsatomic persistence operations or explicit refusal; do not assume readable bytes prove durable naming. Packed content keeps its existing verified pack owner. Do not add a blob-specific publication abstraction, journal, configuration option or framework.
findings.displaced_surface: Displace the loose-blob os.Rename-plus-SyncDirectory publication path with the same fsatomic owner used by pack and backup publishers. Fresh-path-only whole-file AST1184->1180(-4), including return nil; imports unchanged. Existing blobs/commit/fsatomic/Windows tests total2170 unchanged for this substitution, combined5236->5232. This is not a complete repair-cost saving claim: any retry persistence work and its needed test extension are additional and must be counted. No existing assertion/fixture/setup is retired or moved.

findings.title: Bind retention releases to the head of their reachability snapshot

sources.symbol: precheckStore/precheck: sealed backup, isolated candidate, Release, prove, ReplaceStore

findings.evidence: collectLiveSet refreshes the handle, copies aliases/catalog under source.mu.RLock, unlocks, then computes closure. It returns no snapshot head. Release subsequently reads store.Head and uses that later identity as releaseWriter's ExpectedHead. Admitted source counterexample: snapshot H has an aliased rooted artifact R and a releasable orphan O. After the snapshot unlocks, a concurrent Commit on the same handle adds R -> O lineage (known endpoints, no cycle; lineageFacet.validate admits it). Before Release's later Head call, that commit advances the handle to H2. Release binds the old unrooted-O decision to H2; commitCoordinator sees its expected head match, and validateReleases checks only direct alias targets, so O passes although now reachable from R. A concurrent Refresh after another handle's commit has the same effect. writer.commit correctly advances subsequent chunks using its own returned commit ID; the gap is the initial identity. This is source-established interleaving, not an executed test or observed loss.
findings.impact: Potential loss of currently reachable derived content for a Release caller sharing a handle with concurrent writes/refreshes. Current production exposure is limited: the only production caller found, cmd/overgodb.precheck, releases an isolated cloned candidate while the command holds maintenance authority; no current live-store loss is established. Public package Release and Store allow the interleaving and its writer explicitly promises interleaved-writer refusal. No confidentiality, numerical, platform/build-tag or exported-signature change is needed.

device_newton_schulz_normalization.assessment: All owner refinements were applied before the deciding comparison. Supported Windows/CUDA execution required OVERGO_CUDA_TEST=1 and observed execution of both 8+2 FP32 and 4+2 TF32. The 514 scalar comparisons and 56 directions passed bitwise, including guard decisions, normalization multipliers, zero/tiny weights and thresholds around rounded FP32 squared norms. FP64 round-to-nearest scalar instructions were checked despite fast-math compiler options. Twelve alternating pairs across 32 cells compared preservation with reconstruction and counted bandwidth, launches and otherwise-skipped GEMMs. Normal cases ranged from no detectable gain to about 15% faster; every guarded cell was about 105-395% slower. The declared stopping rule rejected the candidate before further full-step/streamed runs. The unchanged production path remains. Optimizer-only gain could have qualified under the frozen 5% minimum, full-step regression and memory limits, but the guard-heavy limit failed. No candidate full-step improvement is claimed.
